overview.oneLineTake: Treat the futures bounce as a relief rally inside a vol expansion: AI credit, 5% yields and $110 Brent keep tails fat, so stay short premium only with defined risk.
themes: AI trade unwind is the dominant driver. QQQ fell 2.5% Friday to 709.80 and SPY lost 1.1% to 763.25 as chip stocks logged their longest losing streak since 2008 and the S&P had its worst week since June.

AI credit stress is now the transmission channel. CoreWeave debt and CDS sit at distress levels, the neocloud selloff is spreading to Nscale, and yields on the lowest-rated corporate bonds are the highest since 2022.
Rates are the ceiling. The 10-year is at 5.10% after a hot September PPI (6.3% y/y), and hike talk is back with the Fed decision looking closer than markets price.
Oil shock layered on top. Brent touched $110 for the first time since May on Red Sea shipping attacks, Iran escalation and renewed Ukraine strikes on Russian energy.
Futures are bouncing on dip buying into a heavy earnings week with Tesla and Meta, while Putin reportedly asked for a summit with Trump and Xi on Ukraine.
risks: Further AI credit events (CoreWeave, neocloud funding) forcing a broader deleveraging in semis and software.
Oil above $110 feeding inflation and pushing yields and hike odds higher.
Mega cap earnings reactions with positioning still crowded in AI leaders.

NDX levels: resistance 29,408 (Thu low), 29,823 (Fri high), 29,936 (Thu close); support 29,073 (Fri low), 29,000.

nq.primaryRisk: Elevated: AI credit and 5% yields drive the volatile downtrend; a bounce failure below 29,073 NDX opens a move under 29,000.

nq.volatility: VIX 20.0 (+21%) and VXN 27.1 (+19%) Friday; vol expanding. Dealer gamma unavailable.

intelligence.headline: US Stock Futures Higher After Bruising Week for Nasdaq
intelligence.summary: US stock futures are higher on the final day of a bruising week. The Nasdaq has shed 3% since Monday as investors grappled with an AI rotation, a sharp rebound in Treasuries and hot inflation.

intelligence.headline: Warsh Silent on Outlook Lifts Odds of October Fed Hold
intelligence.summary: Investors pared bets on an October rate hike after Kevin Warsh was silent on the Fed policy outlook during an appearance in Bangkok.

intelligence.headline: China Moves to Prop Up Stocks With Selling Curbs and Buybacks
intelligence.summary: China moved to stabilize its equity market by urging companies and state funds to buy shares while guiding some investors to curb selling.

intelligence.headline: UK Chancellor Healey Plans Higher Bank Taxes at Budget
intelligence.summary: UK Chancellor John Healey is set to raise taxes on banks to fund cost-of-living support and stabilize the public finances.

intelligence.headline: Tesla Jumps Almost 5% Premarket on Roadster Reveal
intelligence.summary: Tesla shares jumped almost 5% in premarket as the carmaker presented its long-delayed Roadster in a reveal that saw the sports car perform stunts using air thrusters developed with SpaceX engineers.

intelligence.headline: CoreWeave Stock Wipeout Exposes Divide Between AI Fear and Greed
intelligence.summary: CoreWeave plunged 20% in the first three sessions of the week as its debt tumbled to distress levels, with investors pricing more than a 60% chance of default within five years; shares then rallied almost 6% after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said CoreWeave's strength is improving and its cost of capital is decreasing. The stock is up 74% since its March 2025 IPO but down 62% from the June 2025 peak.

intelligence.headline: CoreWeave Co-Founders Have Sold $3.3 Billion in Shares Since IPO
intelligence.summary: CoreWeave's three co-founders have sold $3.3 billion in shares since the IPO.

intelligence.headline: Deutsche Bank Calls CoreWeave Selloff a Buying Opportunity
intelligence.summary: Deutsche Bank says CoreWeave's selloff is a buying opportunity.

intelligence.headline: On the Move: Alcoa, JB Hunt, Brunello Cucinelli
intelligence.summary: Alcoa rose 2% after an earnings beat helped by higher aluminum production and prices. JB Hunt dipped 1.3% on disappointing results and cost pressures. Brunello Cucinelli gained 4.9% in Milan after beating earnings and raising growth guidance. Travelers and Truist Financial report today.

intelligence.headline: Taiwan Fund Managers Quit Jobs to Trade Their Own Money
intelligence.summary: Taiwan's professional stock pickers are barred from owning individual stocks in personal accounts, and with the benchmark up 62% this year (about $1.8 trillion in market cap added), many are quitting for less-regulated trading firms. Fewer than half of the 20 largest local equity mutual funds have kept the same portfolio manager for more than three years.

intelligence.headline: Indonesia Suffers Worst Rout in Decades After MSCI Warning
intelligence.summary: Indonesian stocks suffered their worst rout in nearly three decades after MSCI warned the country's emerging-market status was in jeopardy. Felix Darmawan of PT BCA Sekuritas called it a massive hit to credibility.

intelligence.headline: Wall Street Watches for Bessent Action on Surging Yields
intelligence.summary: Surging US yields are a sore spot for the Trump administration; Wall Street is game-planning for activism from Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent aimed at bringing them down.
